subject: EVALUATE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB400.md - REPAIRED. Every operand that CONSISTS OF a single literal is now treated as a literal, on both sides of the pairing and in a range bound. The former divergence was the SIGN: the sole-literal question rode ConditionBinder.SolePrimary, which answers 8.8.4.7.3 SR2's 'a single data item ... not enclosed in parentheses' and for which a leading sign makes the operand compound, while 8.3.3.3.2 rule 2 puts an ADJACENT sign INSIDE the literal. One helper, two rules, opposite answers. The extraction is the fix: SoleOperand.NumericLiteral is now the ONE 'consists of a single (possibly signed) numeric literal' test, built on the ONE 8.3.3.3.2 rule-2 contiguity test (ArithmeticFormationRules.SignIsPartOfLiteral, previously private to the Table-3 (unary,unary) screen), and it serves 7.3.11.4 GR5 (DEFINE), 13.10.3 SR1 (CONSTANT) and this rule. MEASURED, four programs, all four flipped: `EVALUATE -5 WHEN 6`, `EVALUATE 5 WHEN -6` and `EVALUATE +5 WHEN 6` were ACCEPTED (literal x literal is a blank cell) and are now COBOL1634; the SEPARATED `EVALUATE - 5 WHEN 6` is an arithmetic-expression operand and stays legal, which is what proves the contiguity test load-bearing rather than a blanket sign rule. The CRASH half is gone too: `EVALUATE WS-A WHEN -5` over PIC X(2) bound the object as a computed expression and died at run time ('computed expression in a string context'); it now answers by 8.8.4.2.5 - the integer operand moves, per the MOVE rules, to an item 'of the same length in terms of character positions as the number of digits in the integer', and 14.9.25.4 GR6a drops the operational sign - so -5 participates as the ONE character '5'. The same repair reaches the plain relation (`IF WS-A = -5` crashed identically) and a range bound (`EVALUATE WS-R WHEN -5 THRU -1` over PIC X(2)). One sibling was found and fixed with it: OperandText's numeric-LITERAL arm ignored deSign while the FIELD arm beside it honoured it, so `MOVE -5 TO a PIC X(2)` stored '-5' where `MOVE` of a PIC S9 VALUE -5 stored '5 '; the golden pins the two together. Figurative constants, decimal and floating-point literals classified correctly before and still do.
